newsitem.title: USA: Swiss Bank trucked Nazi gold to Spain, Portugal.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Bank trucked Nazi gold to Spain, Portugal.

text.p: The Swiss National Bank, at the height of the Second World War, sent 280 truckloads of looted Nazi gold to Spain and Portugal in vehicles bearing neutral Switzerland's national emblem, according to a newly discovered U.S. document released on Sunday.

New York Republican Senator Alfonse D'Amato, whose Senate Banking committee has been probing Swiss-Nazi wartime dealings, released the "top secret" document at a news conference, calling it a major archival discovery that deeply embarrasses the Swiss.

"For the first time since our inquiry began we have a document confirming that the Swiss were actively involved in shipping gold for the Nazis. This document proves that the Swiss claim of neutrality was pure nonsense," D'Amato said.
A spokesman for the Swiss Embassy in Washington was not immediately available for comment on the charges.

The document, a Jan. 12, 1946, memo to the head of the U.S. Office of Strategic Services (OSS), the forerunner to the CIA, from an agent in Berne, said that a high-level, but unnamed Swiss source had uncovered a trail of 280 truckloads of gold that the Swiss had sent to Spain and Portugal.

The agent said the gold, allegedly shipped between May 1943 and February 1944, was worth up to two billion Swiss francs ($500 million) at the time. The looted gold likely came from the central banks of occupied Europe and concentration camp victims.
D'Amato said the tonnage of the gold was not known and added that his researchers were searching for documents to see what OSS head William J. Donovan did with this information.

In the memo discovered on Friday by researchers at the U.S. National Archives, the unidentified OSS agent pleaded for a full-scale probe that he wanted to call "Operation Laura" and would include making payments to the top-level Swiss source, the truck drivers and border officials for their testimony.

The Allies had warned Spain and Portugal that they would not tolerate Germany directly shipping gold to the two neutral Iberian nations, thus creating a role for neutral Switzerland to act as a conduit for such shipments.

In late 1946, Switzerland agreed to pay the Allies $60 million in compensation for the looted Nazi gold its banks handled. D'Amato wants that treaty re-negotiated, saying that the Swiss handled gold worth between $400 million and $800 million that the Nazis had looted from the national treasuries of Europe and from concentration camp victims.

D'Amato, accompanied at his press conference by U.S. Jewish leaders and the Israeli secret agent who captured Adolph Eichmann, released a second document quoting the German Reichsbank official in charge of gold shipments as saying that the Swiss routinely trucked gold across Europe for the Nazis.

The Reichsbank official, Karl Graupner, told U.S. military officials after the war that the Reichsbank authorized gold shipments from Switzerland to other parts of Europe, especially Portugal, either by phone or cable. The Swiss then transported the gold in Swiss trucks insured by Swiss insurance agencies with policies paid for by the Reichsbank.

Graupner said that among the officials who authorized such transactions were Emil Puhl, who was found guilty at the Nuremberg War Crimes trials of converting gold taken from death camp victims -- including from their weddings rings, watches and even teeth -- into bullion.

World Jewish Congress Executive Director Elan Steinberg told D'Amato's news conference that some of the gold the Swiss transported in those 280 shipments might have come from concentration camp victims.

"The story of looted Nazi gold is the story of the greatest robbery of all time. They not only plundered the central banks of Europe, they took gold from concentration camp victims," he said, adding that experts estimate that between five and 10 percent of looted Nazi gold came from death camp victims.
